newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures finished the MATIF session marginally firmer, with PIBOR higher too, both amid modest volumes and unswayed by the latest opinion polls, which reinforced a view of the centre-right coalition winning the May/June election, albeit with a reduced majority.

Traders said they expected trading to remain range-bound on Tuesday ahead of the U.S. first-quarter Employment Cost Index release, as the market tries to measure chances of another U.S. interest rate rise at the May 20 Federal Reserve meeting.
Analysts said Wednesday's French bond auction should meet reasonable demand, with 21-23 billion francs worth on sale.

They also said French unemployment figures, although highly volatile and one of the trickiest to predict, could attract some attention given that they come in the middle of a brief campaign before the two-round May 25/June 1 parliamentary election.

Otherwise, the market has taken a calmer stance on France's election for the moment in the absence of opinion polls or other information upsetting the view given by polls so far that the centre-right will return to power, they said.
Economists expect a 0.9 percent rise in the U.S. employment cost index after a 0.8 percent fourth-quarter 1996 rise and say a 1.0 percent first-quarter rise could fuel rate hike fears.
Later in the week come first-quarter U.S. GDP figures, the April National Association of Purchasing Management's index and, crucially, the government's employment and payrolls data on Friday.
As Thursday is a French holiday, the Bank of France will hold a "same-day" securities repurchase tender on Friday instead, a spokesman for the French central bank said.
